messages:
ashwin: Heads-up — saw a noisy-neighbor issue this morning. A single org spiked and pushed latency for a couple of mid-tier customers.

ashwin: Proposal: introduce a lightweight per-org "smoothing" layer that evens enforcement over short windows + a burst-credit bucket so we don't blunt legitimate spikes. Want quick feedback before I sketch an RFC.

maria: Do we have traces/ids for the impacted requests? can we correlate to model size or route?

ashwin: link: https://internal-telemetry/redwood/trace/0x9a7f — it was mostly text-generation routes hitting the hosted pool. small apps on the same pool saw tail latency creep.

jess: +1 to smoothing. My sketch: compute EWMA of tokens/sec per-org over a 60s window, then enforce a soft limit on instantaneous rps using: `effective_rate = max(instant_rps, alpha * ewma + (1-alpha) * baseline)` with a separate burst bucket (token bucket) sized by org tier. This avoids hard drops for short bursts.

jess: Pseudoconfig:
```
quota.enforcement:
  per_org:
    baseline_rps: dynamic
    smoothing_window_s: 60
    smoothing_alpha: 0.2
    burst_bucket_seconds: 30
    burst_multiplier_by_tier:
      free: 0.5
      standard: 1.0
      enterprise: 2.0
```

liam: Curious about fairness: if we smooth based on recent ewma, a noisy tenant could still hog the bucket for a while. Have you considered cross-tenant percentile normalization? e.g., compute each org's 95p over day and limit spikes relative to the cluster 95p distribution.

maria: I worry percentile normalization can be gamed around noisy scheduled jobs. We should also flag patterns: high short-term z-score vs historical baseline. Telemetry should surface both: smoothed rate and z-score anomaly.

ashwin: Good call. How about combining: smoothing + burst bucket for low-latency acceptance, and an anomaly detector that demotes burst_multiplier temporarily if z-score > 4 for X minutes.

jess: That works. For rollout we can do feature flag per-org: `smoothing: on|off` with a control group. Start at 5% of orgs, monitor tokens/unit cost, tail latency, and request drops.

maria: Dashboard queries I'd want up-front:
- per-org ewma_token_rate (60s)
- burst_bucket_level
- zscore_recent_vs_30d
- fraction_of_requests_throttled_by_smoothing
- cost_per_1k_tokens_by_org

jess: I'll add those to the console's per-route observability page under "Quota diagnostics". Add heatmap for top noisy orgs.

liam: One more: make the burst allocation predictable in the API/Console (customers ask why bursts happened). Expose `burst_remaining_seconds` in response headers so SDKs can surface it.

ashwin: Love that. Also need to surface why we demoted burst multiplier in audit logs for compliance.

quota-bot: deploy-preview: quota-smoothing-v1 -> staging (sha: 8f3b1c) :rocket:

jess: I'll take the staging test and add canary script. plan: 5% prod -> 25% -> 100% over 72h if no regressions.

maria: Add an alert: if any org sees throttles > 0.5% of requests AND customer tier == enterprise, page SRE.

liam: One caveat: for Dedicated customers we should skip smoothing by default (they pay for capacity). Make it opt-in for private deployments unless they toggle.

ashwin: Noted. Action items:
- jess: implement enforcement proto + console diagnostics (ETA 3d)
- maria: dashboard and anomaly queries (ETA 2d)
- liam: update API header contract and docs (ETA 2d)
- ashwin: write short RFC + rollout playbook (ETA 1d)

jess: Sounds good. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll add a quick Postmortem note linking this thread for context.

ashwin: Thanks all — I'll draft the RFC now and ping for review.
